text.arabic_uthmani: وَأَنذِرِ ٱلنَّاسَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ فَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ أَخِّرْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ قَرِيبٍۢ نُّجِبْ دَعْوَتَكَ وَنَتَّبِعِ ٱلرُّسُلَ ۗ أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوٓا۟ أَقْسَمْتُم مِّن قَبْلُ مَا لَكُم مِّن زَوَالٍۢ

words.gloss_range: initial conjunction resuming the prior warning scene
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as continuation, so the warning command applies the preceding terror rather than starting a detached topic. Its payoff is the carried-over scene: visual panic becomes speech-directed warning, then arrival, plea, and rebuttal. Messenger rejection, wrongdoer identity, and removal imagery remain contextual pressure, and the recitational variation belongs to the later promise segment rather than to this opening particle.

topics.headline: resumptive warning link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins as an attached continuation of the prior eschatological scene, not as an isolated command.
topics.reason: The particle is aligned as a coordinating conjunction, and the clause evidence links the command to the preceding context.

topics.headline: warning to plea to rebuttal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah architecture moving from warning through plea into rebuttal.
topics.reason: The discourse rows describe a coherent ayah-level movement that the initial continuation helps open.

topics.headline: surah-wide echoes kept contextual
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that messenger rejection, wrongdoer identity, and removal imagery sit behind the verse, while the particle itself only marks continuation.
topics.reason: The echo rows are useful context, but they do not create a separate lexical value for the opening particle.

topics.headline: variant pressure belongs later
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that recitational variation affects the promise segment later in the ayah, not the opening particle.
topics.reason: The row is retained as apparatus because its content points to a later syntactic pressure rather than to the local particle.

words.gloss_range: Form IV imperative commanding active warning of humanity about the arriving Day
words.root_gloss_range: warning, notice, and vowed consequence; locally Form IV selects causative warning
words.prose: {{ar:أَنذِرِ}} ({{tr:andhiri}}) is the governing command of the ayah: one addressed messenger is made responsible for warning all people about the coming scene. The Form IV force makes the warning an act that places hearers under alert, while the wider vow/dedication field is only a supporting pressure around accountability. The command also starts the communication chain later exposed by their promise to answer God’s call and follow the messengers.

topics.headline: singular imperative with universal object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is framed as an assigned warning speech-act aimed at humanity before any subgroup is singled out.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence support an imperative governing the human object and temporal frame.

topics.headline: Form IV causes warning-awareness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command is not bare mention of a future event but making people stand under its danger.
topics.reason: The local Form IV command supports causative warning as the active sense.

topics.headline: warning carries binding consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that warning carries accountability pressure; the vow branch colors duty but does not replace the local warning sense.
topics.reason: The root field supports warning and vow-related pressure, but local grammar selects warning.

topics.headline: warning answered by late promise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a communication chain: warning, divine call, messenger-following, and the later failed response belong together.
topics.reason: The inter-word rows connect the imperative with later quoted obedience claims and other warning imperatives.

words.gloss_range: definite collective human object of the warning
words.root_gloss_range: human sociability, perception, and possible forgetfulness; locally the noun names humanity as warning audience
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّاسَ}} ({{tr:al-nāsa}}) names the warned audience as humanity before the ayah narrows the scene to the wrongdoers. The word keeps the warning public and universal, while the root field of perception and sociability makes the audience morally capable of recognizing the warning. In the surah frame, people are warned here after revelation was sent to bring people from darkness toward the Lord’s path in 14:1.

topics.headline: definite humanity as object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warning first addresses humankind as a whole, not only the condemned subgroup later named.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as definite accusative object of the imperative.

topics.headline: social and perceptive human field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressed humans are beings of recognition and social awareness, though the local noun still simply names people.
topics.reason: The root evidence supports perception and sociability, but local grammar selects the common collective noun.

topics.headline: opening purpose versus closing failure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the surah-frame: people are warned here after the surah opened with people being led out of darkness in 14:1.
topics.reason: The concrete reference row links the human audience here to the surah opening at 14:1.

words.gloss_range: accusative time marker governed by the warning frame
words.root_gloss_range: day and decisive time; locally an eschatological event-time, not a verbal action
words.prose: {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) sets the warning around a specific Day as both the time of encounter and the warned content. The grammar lets the Day hold arrival, speech, and rebuttal in one event-frame, while its nominal root keeps the focus on a decisive occasion rather than vague futurity. The warned Day also exposes their earlier permanence claim, and the arrival formula has parallels at 3:106, 6:158, and 11:105.

topics.headline: warn them of or on the Day
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Day can function as both warning content and temporal setting.
topics.reason: The accusative time noun is locally licensed as adverbial or second object under the warning command.

topics.headline: one Day gathers the scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that time is compressed into a decisive judgment scene, not a calendar date.
topics.reason: The nominal day field and fronted placement support event-time pressure.

topics.headline: Day exposes prior permanence claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warned Day brings together punishment, late negotiation, and their earlier claim of permanence, with formula parallels at 3:106, 6:158, and 11:105.
topics.reason: The rows explicitly link the Day with the arrival formula and the later prior-time marker.

words.gloss_range: imperfect arrival verb with plural object suffix before delayed subject
words.root_gloss_range: coming, arriving, and bringing; locally the punishment comes to them in vivid future presentation
words.prose: {{ar:يَأْتِيهِمُ}} ({{tr:yaʾtīhimu}}) makes the punishment enter the scene as an approaching event attached to them before it is named. The root can include coming and bringing, but the local clause selects vivid arrival, with the delayed subject producing suspense before the punishment is disclosed. That arrival directly defeats the later request for postponement, and it enacts the warning counterpart already sounded in 14:31.

topics.headline: future arrival reaches them first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the recipients before the subject, so the encounter feels unavoidable even before the punishment is named.
topics.reason: QAC marks an imperfect verb with object suffix, and the subject follows after it.

topics.headline: coming with brought-pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the punishment is felt as arriving into their space; broader bringing pressure remains secondary to the local intransitive arrival clause.
topics.reason: The root admits come/bring range, but local syntax has the punishment as the nominative subject that comes.

topics.headline: arrival defeats later postponement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request for postponement is triggered only after the warned arrival has already overtaken them, with 14:31 as a surah-internal warning counterpart.
topics.reason: The contextual rows tie the arrival verb to the later delay request and to 14:31.

topics.headline: motion before subject reveal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the clause first says it comes to them, then reveals the arriver, intensifying suspense.
topics.reason: Verb-subject order and the sound row both support the staged reveal.

words.gloss_range: definite nominative punishment as delayed subject of arrival
words.root_gloss_range: punitive suffering with sensory contrast in the broader root field; locally judicial punishment
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْعَذَابُ}} ({{tr:al-ʿadhābu}}) is the known punishment, grammatically revealed as the subject that comes. Its definite form and nominative role make the scene judicial rather than a neutral disaster aimed at those already identified as wrongdoers. The root field keeps physical suffering and deprivation of relief in the background, and the arrival of punishment produces the belated obedience language that follows.

topics.headline: known punishment as subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a known, warned punishment is the active arriver, not an unspecified hardship.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word definite and nominative as the subject of the arrival verb.

topics.headline: moral recompense with sensory edge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices judicial punishment with bodily affect; the sweet-water contrast sharpens irony but does not change the local sense.
topics.reason: The root evidence supports punitive suffering and sensory contrast, while local context selects punishment.

topics.headline: punishment tied to wrongdoers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that punishment is attached to culpable speakers and produces belated obedience language.
topics.reason: The inter-word rows connect the punishment with those who did wrong and with their later pledge.

topics.headline: approach before naming
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the approach before classification: the clause makes motion felt before the arriving subject is named.
topics.reason: The delayed-subject structure and noun form support punishment as an arriving entity.

words.gloss_range: sequential particle linking arrival to immediate speech
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) locks the wrongdoers’ speech to the arrival of punishment. The particle makes the plea sound reactive and immediate: they speak because the punishment has arrived, not because foresight has matured into obedience.

topics.headline: arrival triggers speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plea follows as an immediate consequence of punishment, not as independent repentance.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence mark the particle as sequential/consequential before the speech verb.

topics.headline: narrative moves into plea
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the scene moves without pause from visitation to quoted response.
topics.reason: The rows make the particle dependent on the following speech event and connect it with the prior boundary.

words.gloss_range: imperfect speech verb opening direct discourse after consequence particle
words.root_gloss_range: saying, utterance, and argument; locally reported speech introducing a plea
words.prose: {{ar:يَقُولُ}} ({{tr:yaqūlu}}) opens the wrongdoers’ direct discourse as one collective utterance after the punishment arrives. The singular verb before a plural subject gathers many speakers into one speech event, and the quoted plea becomes the place where human bargaining collides with the divine retort.

topics.headline: singular verb before plural subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that many wrongdoers are grammatically gathered into one collective utterance.
topics.reason: The verb-before-plural-subject rule supports singular verbal agreement before the plural relative subject.

topics.headline: speech tries to bargain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the saying is not neutral report; it performs a desperate request and obedience offer.
topics.reason: The direct-discourse rows show the plea ordered as address, delay request, and promised obedience.

topics.headline: human plea versus divine retort
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is structured by two voices: human delay and divine recall of their oath.
topics.reason: The discourse rows support the consequential chain and opposing speech pivots.

words.gloss_range: plural relative pronoun whose identity is completed by the wrongdoing clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) delays the speakers’ identity until the following wrongdoing predicate completes it. The form turns the speaking crowd into a determinate moral group, so the plea is heard from people defined by what they had done rather than by social status.

topics.headline: identity waits for the clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers are defined by the following wrongdoing clause, not merely introduced as a crowd.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a relative pronoun completed by the following relative clause.

topics.headline: utterance before moral label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the utterance appears before the moral label fully lands, turning speech into evidence.
topics.reason: The rows support delayed subject placement and moral naming.

words.gloss_range: perfect plural verb completing the relative label of the speakers
words.root_gloss_range: wrongdoing, misplacement, and darkness; locally completed injustice defining the group
words.prose: {{ar:ظَلَمُوا۟}} ({{tr:ẓalamū}}) completes the identity of the speakers as those whose wrongdoing is already accomplished before the judgment scene. The root keeps moral misplacement and darkness together, linking their plea to the surah’s larger movement from darkness toward light. The formula functions as a recurring moral designation at 2:229, 6:47, and 14:44, and their request belongs to the familiar pattern of reprieve pleading that comes too late.

topics.headline: perfect wrongdoing defines speakers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the future scene carries their completed past wrongdoing into their identity.
topics.reason: The perfect verb completes the relative pronoun and marks prior wrongdoing.

topics.headline: injustice carries darkness pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that injustice is not a flat legal label; it carries misplacement and darkness imagery, though the local sense remains wrongdoing.
topics.reason: The root field supports darkness and injustice together, narrowed to the local Form I perfect wrongdoing.

topics.headline: categorical wrongdoer label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the phrase functions as a recurring Quranic designation for morally liable opponents, with examples at 2:229, 6:47, and 14:44.
topics.reason: The formula row gives concrete references and the boundary row connects the label with the preceding terror.

topics.headline: reprieve plea pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that their request participates in a broader pattern of too-late reprieve pleading.
topics.reason: The contextual row explicitly ties the word group to death and judgment pleading contexts.

words.gloss_range: compressed vocative with first-person plural suffix
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, nurture, ownership, and governance; locally direct address to God as their Lord
words.prose: {{ar:رَبَّنَآ}} ({{tr:rabbanā}}) begins the plea with a compressed vocative: they claim “our Lord” relationship at the moment punishment arrives. The suffix makes the address collective and intimate, while the lordship root makes the appeal to care inseparable from the authority that governs deadlines. That claimed intimacy is exposed by the later promise to answer God’s call and follow the messengers, recalling the messenger conflict in 14:13.

topics.headline: vocative without overt call particle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an urgent direct address in which the wrongdoers collectively claim relation to God.
topics.reason: QAC marks a vocative accusative with first-person plural suffix and no overt vocative particle.

topics.headline: care and authority invoked together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that they appeal to sustaining lordship while resisting the deadline governed by that lordship.
topics.reason: The root field supports nurture and authority, locally realized as the title in direct address.

topics.headline: from narrative to direct plea
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this word turns reported narration into direct desperate speech.
topics.reason: The discourse rows support the vocative as the speech-act pivot.

topics.headline: claimed intimacy exposes unanswered call
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pronoun exchange: they claim relation to God while admitting that God’s call and messengers had gone unanswered, with the messenger link recalling 14:13.
topics.reason: The echo rows connect the first-person plural plea with the later second-person call and the messenger context at 14:13.

words.gloss_range: Form II imperative request to postpone the speakers to an endpoint
words.root_gloss_range: delay, lateness, behindness, and after; locally active postponement request
words.prose: {{ar:أَخِّرْنَآ}} ({{tr:akhkhirnā}}) is the hinge of the bargain: the condemned direct an imperative to God asking to be postponed. Form II makes the requested delay active and emphatic, but the object suffix and endpoint phrase show that the delay is bounded, not open escape. The request is paradoxical because they ask to be moved behind the afterlife moment that has arrived, and the delay-to-term formula recalls reprieve wording at 63:10 and 71:4.

topics.headline: imperative with object and endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the inversion: wrongdoers use a command-form toward God while making themselves the object of postponement.
topics.reason: The verb is an imperative addressed to God with first-person plural object and endpoint complement.

topics.headline: delay asks to move behind arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contradiction of asking for delay from the very afterlife moment that has arrived.
topics.reason: The root field supports behindness and afterness, locally narrowed to postponement.

topics.headline: active postponement sought
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form seeks an effected postponement, not a vague pause.
topics.reason: The Form II evidence supports active/intensive postponement.

topics.headline: postponement invokes fixed term
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the request for delay already invokes a fixed term, with formula parallels at 63:10 and 71:4.
topics.reason: The rows explicitly connect the delay root with appointed-term wording and cross-surah reprieve formulae.

topics.headline: return becomes bargaining
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word concentrates the whole impossible bargaining strategy.
topics.reason: The boundary and synthesis rows tie the form, mood, and complement to impossible deferral.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the endpoint of the postponement request
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:ilā}}) turns the delay request toward an endpoint. The particle prevents the plea from sounding like open repentance: it is a movement to a limit, and that limit is named immediately after the demand.

topics.headline: preposition sets temporal boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plea is bounded by an endpoint as soon as the delay is requested.
topics.reason: QAC marks the preposition as governing the following genitive deadline.

topics.headline: direction becomes terminal limit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the requested rescue still moves toward a limit, not outside limits.
topics.reason: The rows tie directional and terminal-limit senses to the prior failed-return boundary.

words.gloss_range: indefinite genitive term governed as the endpoint of postponement
words.root_gloss_range: appointed term, deadline, and deferment; locally a vague requested deadline under a fixed-limit concept
words.prose: {{ar:أَجَلٍۢ}} ({{tr:ajalin}}) names the endpoint as a term, but its indefiniteness makes the request evasively vague. The irony is that asking for a term already invokes appointment and limit, so the requested delay cannot escape decreed timing. The same delay-to-near-term wording appears in 63:10, and the deadline phrase stays within the surah’s wrongdoing-and-accountability frame rather than redefining the noun itself.

topics.headline: some term, not a specified date
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that they ask for some deadline while avoiding a specified accountability point.
topics.reason: The noun is indefinite and genitive after the endpoint preposition.

topics.headline: delay invokes appointment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that their escape language depends on the very idea of appointed limit.
topics.reason: The root field supports fixed term and postponement, narrowed locally to an appointed endpoint noun.

topics.headline: deadline phrase receives qualifier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the formulaic and audible pressure of the indefinite deadline phrase, with the same delay-to-near-term wording in 63:10.
topics.reason: The rows connect the term to its later qualifier and to a concrete cross-surah parallel.

topics.headline: wrongdoing arc kept contextual
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the surah’s wrongdoing arc is relevant context, though it does not define the local deadline noun.
topics.reason: The row is preserved as contextual pressure, not as a lexical claim about the term itself.

words.gloss_range: indefinite adjective qualifying the requested term as near
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, proximity, approach, and offering; locally temporal nearness of the requested deadline
words.prose: {{ar:قَرِيبٍۢ}} ({{tr:qarībin}}) makes the requested deadline sound modest by calling it near, but that nearness undercuts the delay they are asking for. The root can suggest approach or offering, yet locally the adjective qualifies the term and exposes their bargain as a request for just enough time to renegotiate. Because the word closes the delay phrase immediately before the obedience pledge, apparent modesty becomes the bridge into their proposed bargain.

topics.headline: near modifies vague term
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the smallness claim is grammatically attached to the same indefinite deadline.
topics.reason: QAC marks the adjective as genitive indefinite modifying the term.

topics.headline: delay asks distance and closeness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contradiction: they ask to be pushed back while describing the target as near.
topics.reason: The rows explicitly identify the near term as structurally self-undermining.

topics.headline: temporal convenience, not devotion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that nearness here is convenient time, not true approach to God; offering-related pressure remains background.
topics.reason: The broader root field includes approach and offering, but local grammar selects an adjective of temporal nearness.

topics.headline: near closes the delay unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the phrase closes on apparent modesty before the obedience promise begins.
topics.reason: The placement and cadence rows support the closing emphasis.

words.gloss_range: first-person plural jussive promise to answer the divine call
words.root_gloss_range: answering and response, with broader severing/pit imagery in the root; locally active answering of the call
words.prose: {{ar:نُّجِبْ}} ({{tr:nujib}}) begins the promised obedience as a conditional jussive: delay us, and we will answer. The active Form IV reading promises enacted response to the divine call, not mere hearing, and it admits that the call had already preceded their answer. The passive variant can remove speaker agency, while the rare answer-root is shadowed by severing imagery, making the pledge sound marked and fragile at the moment of punishment.

topics.headline: answering depends on delay
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promised answer is grammatically conditional on receiving postponement.
topics.reason: The jussive mood follows the imperative request and governs the call as object.

topics.headline: response paired with call
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that their first reform promise admits the call had already come before their answer.
topics.reason: The rows identify the answer-call pair as a tight formulaic relation.

topics.headline: Form IV enacted answering
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that they promise enacted compliance, not mere hearing.
topics.reason: The local Form IV and first-person jussive support active answering.

topics.headline: variant removes speaker agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a variant reading can shift agency away from the speakers, but the canonical local reading remains active “we answer.”
topics.reason: Variant rows are retained as contrast while QAC keeps the canonical word as first-person active.

topics.headline: rare answer root shadows rupture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promised answer is lexically marked and shadowed by severing imagery, though local grammar selects answer.
topics.reason: The root evidence supports rarity and severing pressure, narrowed to the local answering sense.

topics.headline: rare response tests sincerity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this word is a pressure point for whether the pledge is sincere or transactional.
topics.reason: The rarity and synthesis rows make the promised response a marked point in the exchange.

words.gloss_range: verbal noun object meaning the divine call with second-person suffix
words.root_gloss_range: calling, summoning, invoking, and claiming; locally God’s summons as object of answering
words.prose: {{ar:دَعْوَتَكَ}} ({{tr:daʿwataka}}) makes the promised response specifically about God’s call, not generic religious language. The suffix personalizes the call as Yours, while the root field lets divine summons and the wrongdoers’ own counter-plea collide in the same bargaining sentence. The word contrasts with sincere prayer in 14:40, and because the promised answer is placed before its object, their bargain foregrounds their offer even though the call came first.

topics.headline: Your call as answer object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the call belongs to God and is the direct object they now promise to answer.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verbal noun as accusative object with second-person suffix.

topics.headline: summons meets counter-call
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that they promise to answer the divine summons while making their own plea for delay.
topics.reason: The root field supports call, invocation, and claim, narrowed locally to divine summons.

topics.headline: sincere prayer versus panic pledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a contrast with 14:40: living prayer differs from this panic-driven promise to answer.
topics.reason: The concrete 14:40 row and discourse rows support the contrast.

topics.headline: object follows promised answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the call becomes grammatically answerable only inside their bargain, even though it had preceded their response.
topics.reason: The verb-object and coordination rows support the answer-before-call syntactic pressure.

words.gloss_range: conjunction pairing answering the call with following the messengers
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the second promised reform to the first, making answering the call and following the messengers a paired bargain. The particle gives their offer a balanced shape, but that balance is still conditional on the delay they requested.

topics.headline: two jussives coordinated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pledge has two coordinated parts rather than one vague promise.
topics.reason: QAC marks the conjunction as coordinating the two jussive promises.

topics.headline: call-answer and messenger-following belong together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that response to God and following messengers interpret each other within the bargain.
topics.reason: The semantic and discourse rows support equivalence through coordination.

words.gloss_range: Form VIII jussive promise to follow the messengers
words.root_gloss_range: following, tracking, pursuing, and succession; locally self-involved obedience to messengers
words.prose: {{ar:نَتَّبِعِ}} ({{tr:nattabiʿi}}) is the second half of the pledge: they will follow the messengers if delayed. The Form VIII shape makes the promised following self-involving, while the pursuit branch evokes tracking what they had let pass. The passive variant can remove first-person follower agency, exposing the instability of claimed agency after consequence has arrived.

topics.headline: conditional discipleship promise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that messenger-following is part of the same conditional bargain as answering the call.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as jussive, coordinated with the previous jussive, and governing the messengers.

topics.headline: Form VIII active alignment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that they promise to make themselves followers, foregrounding agency that had expired.
topics.reason: The Form VIII evidence supports self-involved following in the canonical active reading.

topics.headline: variant removes first-person agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a variant reading can depersonalize the following, but the canonical local reading remains first-person active.
topics.reason: Variant rows are preserved as contrast while QAC keeps the canonical active jussive.

topics.headline: following carries pursuit pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that promised discipleship also evokes tracking what they had let pass, though local sense remains obedient following.
topics.reason: The root field supports follow/pursue tension, narrowed to local following.

topics.headline: obedience after sight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this verb crystallizes the critique of obedience promised only after sight.
topics.reason: The synthesis row states the form, mood, and object converge on belated discipleship.

words.gloss_range: definite plural object naming the messenger class
words.root_gloss_range: sending, dispatching, and release; locally known messengers as the object of following
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلرُّسُلَ}} ({{tr:al-rusula}}) names the object of promised following as the messengers, a definite plural category rather than a convenient single envoy. The root keeps divine dispatch in view: to follow them would be to submit to the sent institution they had resisted. The promise echoes earlier refusals to follow messengers at 7:75 and 14:13, while the plural object remains stable even where the recitational form varies.

topics.headline: known plural institution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promise covers the known messenger institution, not one selective messenger.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as definite plural accusative object of following.

topics.headline: messengers as dispatched agents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that messenger-following means submitting to divine dispatch, while release imagery remains background.
topics.reason: The root field supports sending and release, narrowed locally to messengers as sent agents.

topics.headline: warning belongs to messenger line
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the addressed warning and the plural messengers belong to one rejected institution, with the promise echoing refusals at 7:75 and 14:13.
topics.reason: The contextual rows connect this object with the singular warning command and previous messenger rejection.

topics.headline: many envoys compressed as one object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the plural object remains stable even where the phonological form varies.
topics.reason: The form rows support plural compression and variant phonological contrast.

words.gloss_range: compound interrogative-continuative particle opening the rebuke
words.prose: {{ar:أَوَ}} ({{tr:awa}}) turns the scene from human plea to divine counter-question. The compound form both interrupts and reconnects: it arrests the bargaining voice while dragging the speakers back to their earlier oath. Its rebuking force extends through the recalled oath content, not only through the first negated auxiliary.

topics.headline: counter-question opens retort
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the response is accusation, not a request for information.
topics.reason: QAC marks a compound interrogative and conjunction introducing the rhetorical question.

topics.headline: break linked to prior history
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sharp break in speech flow still reconnects the plea to earlier denial.
topics.reason: The form, placement, and sound rows all support interruption plus continuation.

topics.headline: rebuke extends through oath content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question governs the whole recalled oath, not just the first negated verb.
topics.reason: The discourse row describes movement from negated being to oath content.

words.gloss_range: negating jussive particle converting the following imperfect to past denial
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) sets the retort inside remembered negation. By entering before the auxiliary, the particle makes the grammar recall their prior stance rather than open a fresh question about the present.

topics.headline: particle converts imperfect to past negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the retort recalls what they had been claiming, not what they are now asking.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as making the following imperfect jussive with past negation force.

topics.headline: negation controls oath memory
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that denial frames the oath memory from its first syllable.
topics.reason: The placement and sound rows support the compressed accusatory transition.

words.gloss_range: jussive auxiliary under negation framing the oath as a prior state
words.root_gloss_range: being, existence, and state; locally auxiliary statehood in a negated past construction
words.prose: {{ar:تَكُونُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:takūnū}}) makes their oath a state they occupied, not a stray sentence they once uttered. The auxiliary is jussive under negation and governs the perfect oath verb, creating layered past recollection.

topics.headline: negated auxiliary plus perfect complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the oath is embedded inside a remembered state, giving the retort temporal depth.
topics.reason: QAC marks the auxiliary under the negating particle with the perfect oath verb as complement.

topics.headline: arrogance as mode of being
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that their denial is treated as something they were; broader existence-root associations remain background.
topics.reason: The root field supports being and statehood, narrowed to the local auxiliary construction.

topics.headline: being placed under negated recall
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that even the auxiliary form is controlled by the retort’s negating frame.
topics.reason: The row specifically notes the imperfect auxiliary is jussive under negation.

words.gloss_range: Form IV perfect oath verb addressed to the wrongdoers
words.root_gloss_range: swearing, dividing, allotting, and formal commitment; locally completed oath-making
words.prose: {{ar:أَقْسَمْتُمْ}} ({{tr:aqsamtum}}) is the evidentiary exhibit in the retort: the speakers are confronted with their own completed oath. Form IV selects oath-making, while the root’s division and allotment field makes their claim of security sound like a false apportioning of permanence to themselves. Their late obedience pledge is judged against this earlier contrary speech-act, with oath-formula parallels at 6:109, 16:38, and 35:42.

topics.headline: perfect oath inside auxiliary frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices their sworn speech is treated as a completed act inside an already past condition.
topics.reason: QAC marks the perfect second-plural verb as complement of the auxiliary frame.

topics.headline: swearing over false allotment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that their oath of permanence also sounds like a false division or allotment of security.
topics.reason: The root field supports divide/allot and swear, narrowed locally to Form IV oath-making.

topics.headline: formalized declaration by you
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form leaves no distance between the addressed group and the oath they enacted.
topics.reason: The Form IV and second-person suffix rows support formal oath-making tied to the addressees.

topics.headline: late pledge answered by earlier oath
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the new obedience promise is judged against an earlier contrary oath, with oath formula parallels at 6:109, 16:38, and 35:42.
topics.reason: The rows explicitly set their own remembered words against their late pledge.

topics.headline: form and tense converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the oath becomes the proof used against them.
topics.reason: The synthesis and performative rows support the oath as evidentiary exhibit.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking prior temporal source before the recalled oath
words.prose: {{ar:مِّن}} ({{tr:min}}) reaches backward from the panic of the plea into the earlier time of their oath. The preposition makes the retort locate their confidence as prior history, separating present bargaining from the certainty that condemns it.

topics.headline: from before locates oath
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the oath is anchored in prior time, not in the present panic.
topics.reason: QAC marks the preposition as governing the temporal adverbial before.

topics.headline: past confidence split from present request
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle separates their current plea from the earlier confidence that refutes it.
topics.reason: The semantic rows support source and separation values in the local temporal phrase.

words.gloss_range: built temporal adverb meaning before, dependent on the preceding preposition
words.root_gloss_range: before, facing, direction, and acceptance; locally priorness in a frozen adverbial form
words.prose: {{ar:قَبْلُ}} ({{tr:qablu}}) leaves the earlier comparison point implicit: before this. Its built form after an omitted complement makes the retort compact, while the broader root field of facing and acceptance gives a quiet irony to the call they had not accepted before.

topics.headline: before with omitted complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word points backward compactly without spelling out the whole earlier circumstance.
topics.reason: QAC and morphology rows support the built adverbial form after omitted genitive complement.

topics.headline: temporal phrase follows oath verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that prior time is tied directly to the oath accusation.
topics.reason: The temporal noun depends on the preceding preposition and follows the oath verb.

topics.headline: priorness with acceptance irony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that a before-word shares root pressure with acceptance and facing, while the local sense remains temporal before.
topics.reason: The root field supports before, accept, and face, narrowed locally to prior time.

words.gloss_range: negative particle opening the oath content
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the content of the recalled oath as total denial. It controls the possessive-existential phrase that follows, so their oath is not a minor claim but a boast that no removal applied to them at all.

topics.headline: negator governs whole claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the oath content is structured as comprehensive denial from its first particle.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as negating the following possessive-existential clause.

topics.headline: negation performs confidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negation is part of the speech-act by which they boasted of permanence.
topics.reason: The row ties the particle to the recalled sworn boast.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus plural suffix forming the predicate of the negated possession clause
words.prose: {{ar:لَكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) places the addressees inside the predicate before the denied subject is named. Their oath had treated stability as something pertaining to them; the retort pins that false possession claim directly on the group now pleading for delay.

topics.headline: belonging claim before delayed subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the false permanence claim is grammatically attached to them before removal is named.
topics.reason: QAC marks the prepositional phrase with second-person plural suffix as part of the negated existential clause.

topics.headline: stability treated as property
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that they had treated stability as theirs, while the ayah shows that claim revoked.
topics.reason: The semantic and form rows support possessive-dative force tied to the addressed group.

words.gloss_range: emphatic preposition intensifying negation before the indefinite removal noun
words.prose: {{ar:مِّن}} ({{tr:min}}) intensifies the denial before the final noun, making the oath claim not even the slightest removal. Its force depends on the earlier negator, so the two particles work together to make the permanence boast exhaustive.

topics.headline: extra min after negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the oath excludes any instance of removal, down to the smallest case.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as emphatic after negation before an indefinite noun.

topics.headline: nasal surface thickens denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sound and surface weight of the totalizing negation before the final word.
topics.reason: The form and phonetic rows support audible emphasis while the grammar supplies the force.

words.gloss_range: indefinite verbal noun of removal or vanishing closing the negated oath
words.root_gloss_range: cessation, removal, passing away, and shifting from place or state; locally any removal denied by their oath
words.prose: {{ar:زَوَالٍۢ}} ({{tr:zawālin}}) lands the ayah on the very thing the oath denied: removal, vanishing, passing away. As the delayed subject under exhaustive negation, it receives final-position force; as a rare verbal noun here, it makes imagined permanence collapse into the word that names its undoing. Wider root echoes at 14:46 and 35:41 set human claims of permanence against a cosmic impermanence frame.

topics.headline: final noun completes negated clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denied thing is withheld until the end, so removal lands as the final blow.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as genitive after emphatic min and functionally the delayed subject of the negated existential claim.

topics.headline: indefinite under negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the oath denies any instance of vanishing, not one specific fall.
topics.reason: The indefinite verbal noun under negation supports exhaustive force.

topics.headline: motion away and cessation converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that spatial removal and existential passing-away both press against their imagined permanence.
topics.reason: The root field supports removal, cessation, and never-ceasing formula pressure, narrowed locally to the verbal noun in the oath.

topics.headline: judgment disproves no-removal claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the punishment’s arrival directly overturns the claim that no removal could touch them.
topics.reason: The inter-word rows tie the arriving punishment and remembered oath to the final noun.

topics.headline: rare form closes retort
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah closes on a lexically marked vanishing-word, intensifying the irony of denied removability.
topics.reason: The rarity and final-position rows support the word as marked closure.

topics.headline: human permanence set against cosmos
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word concentrates the verdict against imagined permanence, with wider root echoes at 14:46 and 35:41.
topics.reason: The concrete reference row and closure rows connect the rare word with broader impermanence framing.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وَأَنذِرِ ٱلنَّاسَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ ... أَخِّرْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ قَرِيبٍۢ
baseline_models.mechanism: Warning arouses caution before an arriving calamity, while the wrongdoers' first request after its arrival is for temporal deferral. The construction makes warning-time an actionable interval that closes when punishment-time arrives.

activation_trace.role: Warning communicates what is feared in order to awaken caution; it opens the pre-arrival action window.
The day can image a severe event that descends, not merely a calendar date; it marks the threshold.
Arrival gives the punishment directional completion and closes the distance presupposed by warning.
Deferral to a later time is the requested reversal of the completed arrival.
A fixed temporal limit makes the requested extension bounded rather than an escape from judgment.

changed_reading.before: The ayah announces a future punishment and reports a plea for more time.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages a one-way temporal threshold: warning is usable before arrival, but after arrival the wrongdoers can only ask for the action-window to be reopened.

baseline_models.mechanism: The promised change has two linked motions: answer the summons and then travel in the messengers' wake. It is a proposed rerouting of responsiveness and allegiance, not an unspecified promise to behave better.

activation_trace.role: Answering supplies the verbal return that claims to meet the summons.
A call inclines its addressee by speech; it supplies the directive pole of the proposed realignment.
Following as going after another turns verbal response into sustained movement behind a guide.
The messengers and their carried message specify whose path the promised following would adopt.

changed_reading.before: They promise generic obedience if granted a short reprieve.
changed_reading.after: They promise to rewire a whole response sequence: receive the divine summons, return an answer, and continue behind its authorized carriers.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوٓا۟ أَقْسَمْتُم مِّن قَبْلُ مَا لَكُم مِّن زَوَالٍۢ
baseline_models.mechanism: The closing question confronts a former oath that excluded displacement or change. Its temporal priority and binding force make the present request for postponement the audible collapse of a previously secured self-image.

activation_trace.role: The oath is a formally binding assertion, increasing the force of its later contradiction.
Temporal precedence places confident denial before the present scene of compelled recognition.
Removal from place or state gives the denied change spatial, political, and existential breadth.

changed_reading.before: They had denied that they would die or disappear.
changed_reading.after: They had sworn themselves exempt from transfer out of their settled condition; the request for a new term is that oath collapsing under an actual change of state.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier, the messengers describe God as calling the addressees so that He may forgive them and defer them to a named term. The focus plea asks for deferral to a near term and promises to answer that call. The plea therefore requests a replay, in reversed order, of the offer previously refused.

activation_trace.role: The earlier divine call supplies the same summons that the focus speakers belatedly promise to answer.
Protective covering of the fault names the benefit attached to accepting the earlier call.
The earlier offer already contains postponement, making the focus request a demand for a missed provision.
The named limit fixes the earlier postponement within an assigned duration.
The focus answer is the response withheld when the call and postponement were available.

structural_cues: 14:10 sequences call, forgiveness, postponement, and fixed term; 14:44 sequences requested postponement, near term, and promised response.
The same roots for call, delay, and term recur on opposite sides of punishment's arrival.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated lexical chain; I infer that reversed order marks a request to replay a refused offer. A live alternative is simple thematic repetition without deliberate reversal.

changed_reading.before: The plea invents a new bargain under pressure.
changed_reading.after: The plea asks to reactivate the exact call-and-delay arrangement once offered before judgment, but now promises response only after its term has closed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah records a prior completed call-response pair: Satan called and they responded. Their focus promise to answer God's call is therefore not evidence that they lacked responsiveness; it is an attempted reassignment of a faculty already exercised toward the wrong caller.

activation_trace.role: Satan's call supplies the rival summons that actually inclined them in the earlier action-window.
Their completed response proves that answering was active but attached to the rival call.
Blame returns responsibility for that response to the responders rather than the caller.
The self as the person's own identity localizes liability for choosing which call to answer.
The divine call is now named as the object of a belatedly redirected response.

structural_cues: 14:22 has دَعَوْتُكُمْ فَٱسْتَجَبْتُمْ; 14:44 has نُّجِبْ دَعْوَتَكَ.
Both scenes occur in post-judgment speech where blame can no longer be transferred.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an exact rival call-response pair; I infer a contrast in allegiance rather than mere repetition of response vocabulary. Alternatively, 14:22 may establish culpability without being a direct foil to 14:44.

changed_reading.before: They failed to answer and now promise that they would.
changed_reading.after: They did answer a call in life; their plea promises a last-minute transfer of responsiveness from the caller they chose to the Caller they refused.

context_deltas.mechanism: The judgment scene identifies the weak as former followers of the arrogant, while Abraham's speech makes following a relation of belonging. The focus promise to follow the messengers is thus a proposed transfer of social attachment and identity after the old chain of leadership has failed.

activation_trace.role: Their prior position as people going behind human leaders supplies the failed allegiance being replaced.
Claimed greatness and pride characterize the leaders whose following yields no protection.
Following establishes affiliation with the followed, sharpening the identity at stake in the focus promise.
Messenger and carried message identify the authorized alternative to arrogant leadership.
The focus verb proposes entering the messengers' wake after the former following has broken down.

structural_cues: 14:21 explicitly says كُنَّا لَكُمْ تَبَعًا in the same judgment sequence.
14:44 changes only the object of following: from failed human superiors to the messengers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two objects of following and the affiliative use in 14:36; I infer a late transfer of allegiance. The alternative is that each occurrence independently denotes obedience without a social-chain contrast.

changed_reading.before: They promise to start obeying prophetic instructions.
changed_reading.after: They ask to defect from the collapsed follower-chain of the arrogant and enter the messengers' affiliative wake, but only after leadership can no longer be changed.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, the audience is told not to mistake divine postponement for inattention: the wrongdoers are being delayed to a day of fixed gaze and emptied hearts. Their request 'delay us' occurs inside the day to which they had already been delayed, so it asks for a second postponement after the first has been fully spent.

activation_trace.role: Supposition supplies the mistaken reading that postponement means the account has been overlooked.
Inattention is explicitly denied, separating delay from forgotten liability.
Actual divine postponement supplies the already-consumed extension echoed by the focus imperative.
The fixed, raised gaze renders the terminal day as bodily incapacity rather than another deliberative interval.
The heart as empty space supplies the collapse from which the focus plea emerges.
Their imperative repeats the postponement root after its narrated extension has reached its endpoint.

structural_cues: 14:42 يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ is immediately answered by 14:44 أَخِّرْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ.
The intervening body sequence moves from fixed eyes and raised heads to empty hearts before speech resumes.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the immediate root echo and terminal body sequence; I infer that the granted delay is exhausted rather than newly negotiable. A live alternative treats the two delays simply as divine action and human request without a spent-credit relation.

changed_reading.before: They ask for a short first extension once danger becomes visible.
changed_reading.after: They ask for another extension from inside the endpoint of an extension already granted, while the text denies that the earlier waiting ever meant neglect.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah defines the coming day as one without sale or permeating friendship, then as the standing of the account and the rapid settlement of every self. Against that procedural closure, 'a near term' sounds like an attempt to introduce credit or relational leverage into a phase where neither remains operative.

activation_trace.role: Exchange by price is absent on the coming day, removing transactional means of purchasing an extension.
Intimate attachment that permeates the self is also unavailable as relational leverage.
Counting and account define the day as settlement rather than a new performance period.
Speed excludes the slack that the requested near extension tries to recover.
The final account closes the procedural sequence in which the plea is made.
The requested fixed term functions like fresh temporal credit sought after settlement has begun.

structural_cues: 14:31 commands action before the day precisely because exchange and intimate leverage disappear there.
14:41 and 14:51 frame that day by the account, with 14:51 adding speed.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a no-exchange day, a standing account, and rapid settlement; I infer an economic-procedural analogy in the request for a new term. The alternative is a purely temporal plea without a credit metaphor.

changed_reading.before: They ask for a small amount of additional time.
changed_reading.after: They seek fresh temporal credit after the day has become a nonnegotiable settlement, when neither exchange nor relationship can reopen the account.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah repeatedly transfers habitation: opponents threaten expulsion, wrongdoers are destroyed, others are settled after them, and the current audience inhabits the former wrongdoers' dwellings after their fate has been made clear. The oath of 'no removal' is thus spoken from inside material evidence that occupants change while dwellings remain.

activation_trace.role: Expulsion supplies the contested movement out of a claimed land.
Destruction removes the wrongdoers who attempted to control that movement.
Resettlement after the removed people makes habitation explicitly transferable.
Living in predecessor dwellings turns settlement itself into evidence of earlier occupant removal.
Manifest disclosure makes that historical counterexample available rather than hidden.
The denied removal is contradicted by the transfer pattern encoded in the places they occupy.

structural_cues: 14:14 promises settlement after prior wrongdoers; 14:45 says the audience settled in those wrongdoers' dwellings.
14:45 follows the oath-question in 14:44, so the inhabited evidence answers the claim of permanence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies successive removal and resettlement; I infer that continuity of buildings was misread as continuity of occupants. Alternatively, the dwelling notice may function only as historical admonition rather than a direct analysis of زوال.

changed_reading.before: Their oath asserts abstract personal permanence.
changed_reading.after: Their confidence mistakes stable-looking habitation for stable occupancy even while they live inside proof that wrongdoers are removed and their places reassigned.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately after the focus, removal is measured against mountains, and shortly afterward the earth itself is exchanged for another earth. The oath excluding any removal is therefore exposed at nested scales: person, regime, mountain, and world-order all stand inside possible displacement.

activation_trace.role: The immediate recurrence applies removal from place or state to mountains, enlarging the focus root's scale.
A high solid mass supplies the strongest visible benchmark for apparent immovability.
One thing standing in place of another turns cosmic stability into explicit substitution.
The lower world opposed to heaven is itself the object replaced, removing the presumed stable ground.
The oath's denial becomes untenable once the same removal image reaches mountains and earth.

structural_cues: The focus denial مَا لَكُم مِّن زَوَالٍ is followed two ayat later by لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ ٱلْجِبَالُ.
14:48 then replaces the earth and heavens before universal emergence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the immediate root echo and later earth-substitution; I infer a deliberate escalation of scale. The mountain clause may instead quantify the extremity or impotence of plotting, but either reading still destabilizes the oath's scale of permanence.

changed_reading.before: The oath denies only the speakers' death or departure.
changed_reading.after: The oath claims exemption from a displacement that the surah can apply even to mountains and the ground itself; personal permanence fails inside cosmic replaceability.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah gives speech a material ecology: a good word has a fixed root, while a corrupt word is pulled wholly from its root and has no settlement. The focus contains both a former oath of permanence and a new promise of response; context asks whether either utterance has roots in enacted following rather than merely asserting stability.

activation_trace.role: Meaningful speech connecting speakers supplies the verbal entity that receives a botanical structure.
A foundational root supplies the hidden support required for verbal stability.
Durable fixation defines stability as supported persistence rather than verbal insistence.
Whole-root extraction supplies the failure mode of speech lacking a viable foundation.
The absence of fixed settlement names what the corrupt verbal tree cannot secure.
The former oath is a forceful utterance whose claimed permanence can now be tested for rooted support.

structural_cues: 14:24-27 repeatedly binds word, root, fixation, uprooting, settlement, and saying.
14:44 juxtaposes a newly spoken promise with an earlier sworn permanence that events have uprooted.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the word-tree mechanism and two focus utterances; I infer that the mechanism audits the utterances' enacted roots. A live alternative confines the word-tree comparison to its immediate unit and does not project it onto this plea.

changed_reading.before: The earlier oath was simply false and the new promise may be sincere.
changed_reading.after: Both are verbal attempts to claim stability; the surah's word-tree test shifts attention from intensity of speech to whether response and following ever rooted it in action.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah opens with a public movement out of darkness into light and closes by naming itself a delivered communication for people to be warned, know, and remember. The focus imperative is therefore not isolated threat-display; it is the final public exit mechanism offered before arrival.

activation_trace.role: Passage to the outside gives the message an intended movement away from enclosure.
Illumination supplies the destination in which danger and route become visible.
Delivery of a message frames the surah as communication that reaches its public.
The closing warning repeats the focus function of awakening caution through feared consequence.
Knowledge as disclosure names the cognitive change warning is meant to produce.
Bringing something back into active awareness completes warning's intended uptake.
The focus command occupies the surah-wide communication pathway from disclosure to caution.

structural_cues: The مخاطب الناس of 14:44 is enclosed by الناس in the opening exit-program and closing proclamation.
The closing sequence links delivery, warning, knowledge, and remembrance as successive uptake functions.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies opening movement and closing communication functions; I infer that warning is an offered exit rather than spectacle alone. The alternative is that opening and closing are broad framing devices without a specific mechanism for 14:44.

changed_reading.before: The command asks the messenger to frighten people with a future scene.
changed_reading.after: The warning is the surah's last public route from enclosure to disclosed knowledge and remembered caution before the arriving day makes voluntary exit impossible.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the sweet-water and abstention branches of ع ذ ب rather than replacing the ordinary punishment branch. It remains anchored in the focus noun and in 14:16-17's explicit administered water that cannot be swallowed. Downstream prose should present it only as a sensory counter-image within this surah, not as an etymological redefinition of punishment.

activation_trace.role: Potable sweetness supplies the positive water-pole that the punishment scene materially reverses.
Abstention from food or drink supplies the bodily non-intake realized when liquid cannot become drink.
Giving drink supplies the forced watering action.
Water itself supplies the expected medium of refreshment.
Smooth passage through the throat is nearly impossible, converting water into blocked intake.
Painful punishment names the dominant sense while the water branches supply its sensory inversion.

changed_reading.before: Punishment is an abstract penalty that arrives.
changed_reading.after: Within this surah's material staging, punishment also feels like anti-watering: liquid is administered yet denied the smooth, life-serving passage expected of drink.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain juridical reading assembled from focus branches for withheld right, claim, liability, oath, and fixed term, then sharpened by the final account. It remains anchored in several focus constructions, but the ayah does not explicitly call itself a court proceeding. Downstream prose should mark it as a legal-mechanism analogy, not a syntactic determination.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ... أَجَلٍۢ ... دَعْوَتَكَ وَنَتَّبِعِ ... أَقْسَمْتُم

activation_trace.role: Withholding or confining a right casts wrongdoing as an unresolved liability.
A fixed term supplies the deadline after which the liability matures.
Assertion of a right supplies a summons-like edge to the call they promise to answer.
An attached consequence or liability makes following carry what trails an earlier act.
The oath supplies a prior binding representation now contradicted by the speakers' position.
Exacting and settling a debt supplies the terminal collection mechanism.
The account gathers the acts into a closed reckoning.

changed_reading.before: The wrongdoers make an emotional appeal for another chance.
changed_reading.after: The plea can be carried as an attempt to reopen a closed case after its fixed term: answer the summons now, assume the proper liability now, despite the prior oath and matured account.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant ق ل ل mapping for focus ق و ل, especially its shudder and instability branches. It remains formally anchored to يَقُولُ and gains contextual support from fixed sight and emptied hearts immediately before the speech. Downstream prose must label it a consonantal branch activation, not the lexical meaning of يقول.

activation_trace.role: Shudder and agitation recast the utterance as a bodily symptom of fear.
Instability and movement make the speech itself register the collapse of their non-removal claim.
A fixed, protruding gaze supplies the body's arrested visual state before speech.
Interior emptiness supplies the affective void from which the plea breaks out.
Movement and agitation after stillness invert the speakers' former denial of any destabilization.

changed_reading.before: Their plea is a composed verbal proposal.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the saying is also the first tremor of the permanence they had asserted: fixed eyes, emptied hearts, and destabilized speech expose the oath bodily.

strongest_changes: 14:10 makes the plea a reversed replay of an earlier call, forgiveness, postponement, and fixed term that had been refused.
14:22 shows that they did answer a call, but the wrong one; 14:21 likewise shows that they followed, but the wrong leaders.
14:42 makes their requested delay a second extension sought from inside the endpoint of delay already granted.
14:45-48 answer the oath of no removal with transferred dwellings, potentially moving mountains, and a replaced earth.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context turns nearly every promise in 14:44 into a reversal of an earlier exercised choice: call was refused, response and following were misdirected, delay was spent, and permanence was asserted while predecessor dwellings and the created order displayed replaceability.
remaining_uncertainties: The mountain-removal clause can scale either the force or the impotence of plotting, though both readings destabilize claimed permanence.
Applying the rooted-word mechanism of 14:24-27 directly to the oath and plea in 14:44 is coherent but not explicit.
The anti-watering, closed-case, and speech-tremor models depend on branch-distant or cross-domain activation and should remain exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Warning attempts to import the future plea into the present response window.** `ن ذ ر` `B001` awakens fear, `ء ت ي` `B001` is arrival, `ء خ ر` `B002` deferral, `ء ج ل` `B001` fixed limit, `ج و ب` `B003` response, and `د ع و` `B001` call. The ayah quotes a future request to answer. I infer warning's mechanism is temporal transfer: hearing now can perform the response that cannot secure more time later. The command reads as anticipatory relocation of decision.

2. **Claimed permanence is exposed as refusal to imagine state-change.** `ق س م` `B004` is an oath apportioned among holders; `ز و ل` `B001` is departure from place/state and `B008` continued state under negation. The ruined dwellings in the next ayah directly refute the oath. I infer collective swearing distributes and reinforces a false permanence claim. The ending reads socially as mutually guaranteed denial.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The inhabited ruins of 14:45 immediately refute the oath of permanence: the addressees occupy material proof that prior occupants did, in fact, depart from their state.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The warned event overtakes rather than merely arrives.** `ن ذ ر B001` supplies warning that awakens fear, and `ء ت ي B011` supplies being overtaken by ruin alongside ordinary arrival (`ء ت ي B001`). The punishment is grammatical subject coming to them; 14:45 supplies ruined predecessors' dwellings and 14:49 criminals already bound. The packet supplies approach and capture; I infer that the day closes distance until its subjects are overtaken. `يَأْتِيهِمُ ٱلْعَذَاب` reads as active interception.
2. **The request is belated temporal bargaining.** `ء خ ر B002` supplies postponement, `ء ج ل B001` a fixed term, and `ق ر ب B002` temporal nearness. 14:42 explained that God had already deferred them to a day; once it arrives, they ask to insert one more near term. The packet supplies original delay and requested redelay; I infer an attempt to renegotiate the boundary only after its protection expires. `أَخِّرْنَا` reverses their earlier interpretation of delay as heedlessness.
3. **Response and following are offered only after evidence becomes coercive.** `ج و ب B003` supplies answering, `د ع و B001` calling near, and `ت ب ع B001` following. In 14:39-41, prayer, hearing, acceptance, and faith precede the day; here the promise to answer and follow occurs after punishment has arrived. The packet supplies the timing contrast; I infer that visibility has removed the open response condition. Their words describe the right acts at the wrong causal stage.
4. **The no-departure oath is overturned by actual displacement.** `ز و ل B001` supplies departure from a place or state. The speakers had denied any `زَوَال`; 14:46 says their schemes could aim to move mountains, and 14:48 replaces earth with other earth. The packet supplies claim, attempted movement, and actual transformation; I infer that asserted permanence was attached to the wrong agent and substrate. `مَا لَكُم مِّن زَوَال` reads as a failed theory of stability.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 14:46 and 14:48 overturned the prior no-departure oath through attempted mountain movement and actual world transformation. By 14:49 the warned subjects were visibly bound, confirming `ء ت ي B011` as being overtaken rather than mere arrival.

baseline.text: İnsanları azabın kendilerine geleceği gün konusunda uyar. O zaman zulmedenler, “Rabbimiz, bize kısa bir süre daha ver de çağrına cevap verelim ve elçilere uyalım” derler. “Daha önce yok olup gitmeyeceğinize yemin eden siz değil miydiniz?”

findings.text: Uyarı, gelecekteki pişmanlık sözünü bugüne taşıyarak sonra zaman kazandıramayacak cevabın şimdi verilmesini amaçlar.
Azap yalnız gelmez; aradaki mesafeyi kapatıp muhataplarını yakalayan etkin bir olay olur.
Daha önce verilmiş erteleme bittikten sonra yeni ve yakın bir süre istemek, koruyucu zaman sınırını ancak kapandığında yeniden pazarlık etmektir.
Yok olmayacaklarına ilişkin yemin, kalıcılığı yanlış özneye ve değişmez sanılan bir dünyaya bağlayan başarısız bir istikrar kuramıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişiye ya da topluluğa korkulacak bir durumu bildirip onları sakınmaya uyandırma anlamıdır. Uyaran kişi, uyarı olayı, karşılıklı uyarma ve tehlikeyi öğrenip korunmaya geçme kullanımları bu çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

facets.statement: Bir kişi ya da topluluğa korkulacak bir durumu haber vererek onları sakınmaya yöneltir.
Aynı çekirdek, uyaran kişi veya uyarı olayının kendisi için adlaşmış kullanımlara taşır.
Topluluk içinde birbirini tehlikeye karşı uyarma, çekirdeğin karşılıklı eylem biçimidir.
Düşmandan haberdar olup hazırlık ve korunmaya geçme, bilginin sakınma sonucunu gösterir.
Ani tehlike habercisi ve ordunun öncü gözcüsü gibi sözler, uyarı çekirdeğine bağlı örneklerdir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Verilen komşuların tümü gözden geçirildi; yara karşılığı, kan bedeli, yüklenme, bedelsiz kalma ve aynı kök içi adak ayrımı en belirgin sınırları verdi.

root_profile.summary: Bu kök çok dallı bir yapı gösterir: tehlikeyi bildirerek sakındırma, kişinin kendine adak yükümlülüğü koyması ve yaralama için ödenmesi gereken karşılık ayrı çekirdeklerdir. Dallar, uyarı iletişimi, gönüllü bağlanma ve hukuki bedel eksenlerinde ayrılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşısındaki insan türünü, bu türün topluluğunu ve tek bir üyesini birlikte gösterir. Görünür olma açıklaması adlandırma gerekçesidir; insan olmanın kurucu tanımı değildir. Evde kimsenin bulunmadığını bildiren kalıp ise dal çekirdeğine genellenemez ve yalnızca kendi sözcüksel biriminde korunmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, insan türünü ve onun tekil ya da toplu üyelerini kapsar; yakınlık duygusunu, duyusal algıyı ve insana dönük yanı kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak biçimlerdeki insan ve insan topluluğu anlamı dal çekirdeğidir; evde hiç kimse bulunmadığını anlatan kalıp ayrı tutulur ve çekirdeğe yeni bir genel anlam katmaz.

concept_map.definition: Görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşısında yer alan insan türünü, bu türün topluluğunu ya da tek bir üyesini belirtir. İnsanların görünür oluşu, bu adlandırma için aktarılan bir gerekçedir.

facets.statement: İnsan türünü, insanların oluşturduğu topluluğu veya bu türün tek bir üyesini görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşısında adlandırır.
Adlandırmanın insanların duyularla görünür oluşuna bağlanması, anlamın özü değil kökene ilişkin bir açıklamadır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarımlar, dalın insan türünü hem topluluk hem tek kişi olarak gösterebildiğinde ve görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfıyla karşıtlık kurduğunda birleşir. Görünürlük, ortak anlamdan çok adlandırmanın gerekçesi olarak sunulur.

concept_gloss.text: insan türü ve bu türden bir kişi
concept_gloss.applicability: İnsanları bir tür veya topluluk olarak anlatırken de bu türün tek bir üyesini belirtirken de kullanılabilir.

error_profile.preserves: İnsan türü ile onun tekil üyesi arasındaki kapsamı ve temel sınıf karşıtlığını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Türün üyeleri topluca veya görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşıtı olarak anıldığında doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: İnsan türünün toplu olarak adlandırılmasını açık ve doğal biçimde korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bağlam türün tek bir üyesini veya herhangi bir kimseyi gösterdiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: İnsan topluluğundan tek bir üyenin belirtilmesini korur.

belirli bir ağızda insan ve onun çoğulu

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, insanı görünür ten ve yaratılmış beden yönüyle adlandırır; tekil, çoğul, erkek ve kadın kapsamını özellikle öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: insan türünü iki ayrı yönden adlandırma
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da insanı hem tür hem bu türün üyesi olarak gösterebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Yer değiştirme yalnız insanı genel olarak adlandıran bağlamlarda mümkündür. Odak dalın görünmeyen varlıklarla sınıf karşıtlığı, komşunun ise görünür beden yönü kendi sınırında kalır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal yalnız insan türünü ve bu türün tekil ya da toplu üyelerini belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yeryüzündeki bütün yaratılmışları kapsayabilir ve bazı yorumlarda insanlarla görünmeyen varlıkları birlikte içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: insan türü ile bütün yaratılmışlar ayrımı
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İnsanlar iki dalın gönderim alanında da bulunabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşunun genel yaratılmışlar kapsamı odak dala taşınamaz; odak dal da yalnız insanları belirttiği için bütün yaratılmışların yerine kullanılamaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal insan türünü ve bu türün üyelerini adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal yabancılık ve ürkme duygusunun kalkmasını, yakınlık ve rahatlık oluşmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: insan adı ile yakınlık duygusu ayrımı
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da insan, temel gönderim noktası veya deneyim sahibi olabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Birinde insanın kim olduğu adlandırılır, diğerinde bir kişi ya da şey karşısındaki duygusal durum anlatılır; sıradan bağlamlarda birbirlerinin yerine geçmezler.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün aday kartlar karşılaştırıldı. Yalnız insanı adlandırma sınırını yaratılmışlar kapsamından ve yakınlık duygusundan ayıran, okuyucu için en yararlı üç karşıtlık yayımlandı.
